speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (a) for an update on the implementation of key initiatives under the National Mental Health and Well-Being Strategy since its launch in 2023; (b) whether time-bound targets, baselines or KPIs have since been established; and (c) how the Government assesses whether the strategy is on track to achieve its intended outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: First, we have guided our mental health service providers to operate based on the Tiered Care Model.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: Clients can now receive care at the most appropriate setting to better meet their needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: We are also standardising mental health assessments and referral pathways to improve care coordination across different providers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: Second, we have expanded the capacity of mental health services across the acute, primary, community and long-term care sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: We have also established the First Stop for Mental Health services such as our national mindline 1771 to help people navigate and access services more easily.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: Fourth, we have promoted mental health and well-being through our education efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: These include Parenting for Wellness to empower parents with knowledge and skills to support their children’s mental health needs, and the Positive Use Guide which offers practical tips to the public to use technology and social media in a healthy and balanced way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: Lastly, we have strengthened workplace mental health support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: The Ministry of Manpower has worked with the Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) Council to implement initiatives that build employers’ competencies in supporting employees’ mental well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: In addition, the WSH Council launched the Handbook on Supporting Employees' Mental Health last year.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I have two supplementary questions for the Senior Minister of State, the first relates to the NMHO.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I noted that in last year during the Committee of Supply, it was stated that the NMHO tracks the mental health data internally.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Will the Government commit to publishing these outcomes and indicators externally, for instance, through a public dashboard, similar to Australia's Mental National Mental Health Performance Framework?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: This will allow Parliament and the public to be able to better assess whether the strategy is on track through measurable and regularly updated indicators that are published.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: And my second supplementary question relates to measurable outcomes and the impact on the treatment gap.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Beyond the listing of initiatives, my supplementary question relates to what measurable outcomes have been observed since the strategy is launched in 2023?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: For example, rates of self harm, suicide attempts or help seeking behaviours.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I note that in 2016, there was a treatment gap with approximately 78% of individuals with conditions not seeking treatment.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: And if not, how does the Ministry assess progress towards measuring and narrowing this gap?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We will look at how we can meaningfully share more data publicly over time.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But I must say that the strategy, while we had launched it towards the end of 2023, it has only been slightly just more than two years.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mental health is a very complex and multi-faceted issue, so you can see from our strategy we are trying to put more resources into the public domain so that those with mental health issues or concerns can have more accessibility to those resources that we put out.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The Member will understand that for those suffering from mental health issues, it sometimes takes quite a while to convince them to seek help.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, it is not so easy for us to measure outcomes in such a short timeframe.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In time to come, when we have more meaningful data that we can share publicly, we will do so.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Also, through the Tiered Care Model, we then make sure that they receive the appropriate care.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Based on this early set of strategy, we will continue to measure indicators and in time to come, share data where available.
